headline: A California law firm has filed a proposed class action accusing Thomson Reuters of buying the cheaper AI legal-research rival Casetext to remove a competitor.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 6: the complaint was filed 1 Oct 2026 (before 2 Oct) and holds only one law firm's allegations that no court has tested.
importance_line: If a court lets it go ahead, it could affect lawyers who pay for legal-research tools and Thomson Reuters, and it tests whether buying an AI start-up mainly to shut down a rival counts as illegal; for now these are one firm's claims and no court has ruled.
summary: The ABA Journal reports that the Rubin Law Office filed the complaint on 1 Oct 2026 in a federal court in Northern California, alleging that Thomson Reuters bought Casetext for $650 million and folded it into its more expensive Westlaw service, so the firm's own cost rose from $32.50 to $111.48 a month. These are the plaintiffs' claims only, and a Thomson Reuters spokesperson told Bloomberg Law that the company had not been served with any complaint.
notes: Original outlet Law360 (paywalled); written from the ABA Journal report of the same complaint. Event dated 1 Oct 2026, so marked as before the 2 Oct cut-off and scored one lower.
